processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Iron powder (700 g) and ferrous oxalate (FeC2O4·H2O, 1.575 g) placed in an alumina crucible and heated in a tubular furnace to 1873 K.
225 g ferromanganese added (as deoxidizer) and held for 20 min.

processing_steps.method: aluminum addition (wrapped in pure iron sheet)
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: 11 g aluminum particles wrapped in pure iron sheet added and held for 60 min (first group addition mass = 11 g).
Finally, the sample was cooled to room temperature in a tubular furnace.

structures.overall_structure: As-cast Fe-15Mn-1Al-C low-density steel containing non-metallic inclusions (single Al2O3, AlN, MnS, TiN particles and Al2O3-MnS, AlN-MnS, TiN-MnS, Al2O3·AlN·MnS composite inclusions).

microstructure_list.region: bulk (as-cast steel matrix and inclusion population)

inclusions.name: Al2O3-MnS
inclusions.morphology: inner and outer layers (dark Al2O3 core enclosed in lighter MnS)

inclusions.name: AlN-MnS
inclusions.morphology: clustered dark AlN particles attached to an MnS particle
inclusions.notes: Figure 1g shows the element surface distribution of AlN-MnS inclusions.

inclusions.name: TiN-MnS
inclusions.morphology: dark TiN attached to lighter MnS with a visible interfacial boundary
inclusions.notes: Clear interfacial relationship between MnS and TiN inclusions is observed.

inclusions.name: Al2O3·AlN·MnS
inclusions.morphology: 3D morphology showing AlN, MnS and Al2O3 regions

defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: A clear interfacial relationship between MnS and TiN inclusions is observed in the TiN-MnS composite inclusion.
Al2O3, AlN, and TiN could provide nucleation sites for MnS, and Al2O3 could also provide heterogeneous nucleation sites for AlN (mismatch degrees 8.41%, 8.94%, 11.65%, 11.66%).

interfaces.phase_evolution: Solidification route of 1#: L → L + FCC → FCC.
interfaces.interface_notes: Mismatch degrees of Al2O3/MnS, AlN/MnS, TiN/MnS, and AlN/Al2O3 are 8.41%, 8.94%, 11.65%, and 11.66%, respectively, all in the moderate effective zone (6–12%).

characterization_methods.technique: Field-emission scanning electron microscopy (FE-SEM) with energy dispersive spectrometer (EDS)
characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: ZEISS ΣIGMA HD with Oxford-X-Max 50 mm²
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Mirror-polished metallographic samples and nonaqueous-solvent electrolytically extracted inclusion powders; Figure 1 panels a–i with scale bars (mostly 4 μm, panel h 5 μm).
characterization_methods.purpose: Observe morphology and type of inclusions in 1# sample
characterization_methods.key_findings: 1# sample contains single Al2O3 (elongated, length >8 μm), AlN (elliptical; extracted elongated AlN ≈12 μm), MnS, TiN (angular), and Al2O3-MnS, AlN-MnS, TiN-MnS, Al2O3·AlN·MnS composite inclusions.

characterization_methods.purpose: Detect size, type, and number of inclusions
characterization_methods.key_findings: 1# sample inclusion size distribution: 1–5 μm 58.4%, 5–10 μm 32.3%, >10 μm 9.4%.

characterization_methods.technique: Chemical analysis methods (carbon-sulfur analyzer; inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry)
characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Carbon-sulfur analyzer (T.O, T.N, C, S); inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (Al, Si, Ti, Mn, P)
characterization_methods.purpose: Determine chemical composition of the steel

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Electric discharge wire-cutting machine; metallographic sandpaper and polishing paste
characterization_methods.purpose: Prepare mirror-surface samples for inclusion observation

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Magnet for separating inclusion particles from ethanol-containing solution; carbon strip collection
characterization_methods.purpose: Prepare inclusion powder for SEM/EDS observation

computational_details.simulation_method: CALPHAD phase diagram calculation (FactSage 8.2 phase diagram module)
computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: 1# alloy composition from Table 2 (C 0.41, Si 0.32, Mn 14.85, Al 0.868, N 0.0032, P 0.043, S 0.014, O 0.0005, Ti 0.0057 mass%, Fe Bal.); vertical section at C ≈ 0.4 wt%.
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: 1# liquidus 1702 K, solidus 1588 K; solidification route L → L + FCC → FCC.

computational_details.simulation_method: Clyne–Kurz microsegregation model combined with equilibrium thermodynamics (logK vs logQ intersection)
computational_details.potential_model_or_database: Interaction coefficients from Table 4; equilibrium distribution coefficients k and diffusion coefficients D from Table 5; T0 = 1809 K.
computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Equations (1)–(14) for AlN, (15)–(18) for TiN, (19)–(22) for MnS; cooling rate R_C; 1# composition as initial content.
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Computed solidification fractions of inclusion precipitation in 1#: AlN 0.46, TiN 0.89, MnS 0.77.

analytical_models.equation_role: Theoretical concentration product of AlN in 1# sample
Theoretical concentration product of TiN in 1# sample
Theoretical concentration product of MnS in 1# sample

computational_details.potential_model_or_database: Lattice parameters from Table 6: AlN a=b=3.110, c=4.980 Å; MnS a=b=c=5.224 Å; Al2O3 a=b=4.759, c=12.991 Å; TiN a=b=c=4.242 Å.
computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Equation (23); low-index lattice planes/directions from Table 7.
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Computed mismatch degrees: Al2O3/MnS 8.41%, AlN/MnS 8.94%, TiN/MnS 11.65%, AlN/Al2O3 11.66%.

analytical_models.equation_role: Assess heterogeneous nucleation effectiveness of Al2O3, AlN, TiN substrates for MnS and Al2O3 for AlN

unmapped_findings: 1# sample measured chemical composition (mass%): C 0.41, Si 0.32, Mn 14.85, Al 0.868, N 0.0032, P 0.043, S 0.014, O 0.0005, Ti 0.0057, Fe Bal. (Table 2, b0020/b0025/b0026).
1# sample inclusion size distribution: 1–5 μm 58.4%, 5–10 μm 32.3%, >10 μm 9.4% (b0033, Figure 5).

In Figure 4 (1# sample), the Al2O3 segment is roughly one-third of the stacked bar and AlN roughly one-tenth; the four composite-inclusion segments occupy roughly the upper quarter to third (figure_004).
A large number of single-particle Al2O3 inclusions are formed during the smelting process when the Al content is 1% (i.e., the 1# sample) (b0111).
Precipitation order of single-particle inclusions in the steel: Al2O3 > AlN > MnS > TiN (b0107).
